key_evidence_spans: His heart rate remained between 60 and 100 bpm;
His mother had systemic lupus erythematosus treated with hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisolone and was positive for anti-SSa/Ro and anti-SSb/La antibodies.
On day 14, antibody testing confirmed high-titer antinuclear antibodies (>1:1000) and 52-kD anti-SSa/Ro and anti-SSb/La positivity.
A permanent pacemaker was placed on day 50, with transient clinical improvement.
A chest CT on day 36 showed bilateral areas of diffuse ground-glass opacity and air bronchograms.
Inflammatory markers remained normal, cultures were repeatedly negative, and a follow-up chest CT demonstrated progression of the bilateral ground-glass opacities.
